content.title: About
content.content: Raw clams are marine bivalve mollusks that live in coastal waters of seas and oceans. They have tender meat, a mildly salty flavor and a distinct sea aroma. Raw clams are often used in sushi, ceviche and as a component of cold appetizers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Clams filter water, helping to clean it of microscopic particles.
There are over 500 species of clams, but culinary use focuses mainly on members of the Veneridae family.
Clams can close their shells tightly to protect themselves from predators and adverse conditions.
In some cultures clams are considered a delicacy and are served in special ceremonies.
Clams can regenerate tissue, making them interesting subjects for biomedical research.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Clams provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many seafood items, clams contain very little fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system function and blood formation; clams are one of the best natural sources.

items.title: Rich in minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: Clams supply iron for oxygen transport and zinc to support immune health.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of omega‑3 in clams help promote heart health.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw clams may harbor pathogenic bacteria and viruses (e.g., Vibrio), so consumption requires caution.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to clams, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy metal accumulation
items.content: Clams can accumulate toxins such as cadmium and mercury, especially in polluted waters.

items.title: Not recommended for pregnant women
items.content: Due to the risk of bacterial contamination, pregnant women should avoid raw clams.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw clams are typically served chilled, thinly sliced, with soy sauce, lemon, ginger or wasabi. They are also used in ceviche, where the acid “cooks” the meat. Before serving, rinse clams thoroughly in cold water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store clams in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C in a tightly sealed container covered with a damp cloth. Use within 1‑2 days. Discard any clams that remain open and do not close when gently tapped.
